text:
maria: Ran a focused nsys trace on the high-p95 tail we saw on nightly load. Repro steps: 10k short-chat requests (seq len 64), continuous batching on, kv-cache warm, 8xA100. Observed a recurring ~12ms queue spike right before the main matmul kernel that correlates with a kernel-selection path switch.

jeff: can you paste the timeline? was that during burst or steady-state?

maria: steady-state after warmup. attaching clipped timeline from the run below. Note the narrow window where kernel selector falls back to the generic GEMM path.

maria: ```
# nsys timeline snippet (condensed)
0.000s  request enqueue
0.001s  kernel: compute_kv_cache_lookup (0.3ms)
0.002s  kernel: select_kernels (0.05ms)
0.014s  kernel: generic_matmul_launch (10.8ms)  <-- long compute + queue gap
0.027s  kernel: attention_opt (0.8ms)
```

eli: weird that select_kernels is tiny but we still end up with generic_matmul. That suggests the selector chose a variant with non-optimal tile/kernel because of input dims or a quantization flag.

anna: I also saw a KV cache sweep happening right before that in some runs. Could be eviction/resync causing a short CPU stall that delays the preferred kernel's CUDA context setup.

nsys-bot: Uploaded full capture to /shared/traces/1811234567_nsys_capture.qdrep (12MB). nvprof metrics: SM_efficiency drop ~22% in affected windows.

jeff: If it's a tiny CPU-side stall shifting the enqueue time we can end up missing the batched launch slot and get an extra kernel setup latency. What's our batching window config?

maria: continuous_batch.window_ms=3, max_batch=16. The spike aligns with occasional requests that have a KV cache miss path that takes ~1.5ms on CPU (lock + deserialization). That can push a request out of the tight window.

eli: hypothesis: selector ranks kernels by expected runtime + launch overhead; when request misses and triggers cache work, the estimated runtime changes and selector picks a fallback path (generic_matmul) because it assumes different shapes or fallback dtype.

anna: reproducer idea: force a controlled KV miss on a subset while running steady batching. Compare kernel choices and queue times with perfetto to see if scheduler gaps line up with cache activity.

maria: did a quick A/B yesterday: with KV-miss injection on 5% of requests p95 goes from 18ms -> 32ms. Without injection p95 stable at 18ms. Difference: extra 9-14ms queue+setup.

jeff: ok action items: 1) add micro-trace hook to log selector decision vector and cache state per request (lite log). 2) bump continuous_batch.window_ms to 6ms in canary to see smoothing effect. 3) check kernel binary selection thresholds for small windows.

eli: tiny note — if we just increase window_ms we may increase token cost per request due to larger batches, but will likely reduce tail. Worth running cost/latency trade simulation.

maria: started a canary with window_ms=6 on a 10% route. so far tail dropped ~6ms in the first 2000 requests. full nsys capture uploaded as 1811234600_canary.qdrep.

infra-bot: Canary rollout: route "chat-short-canary" -> 10% (start 2025-09-04T11:13:40Z). Monitoring p95 and error rate.

jeff: also double-check kernel cache warming: real kernels are JIT+PTX path compiled/loaded lazily. If the preferred kernel isn't resident due to previous evictions, we might see first-use overheads mid-run. Add a prewarm step after reconfig or model swap.

maria: noted. Will add a lightweight 'ensure_kernels_loaded()' after quantization profile selection. Also adding a metric for 'kernel_variant_used' to trace logs.

anna: for debugging, here's a short diff that dumps selector state (pseudo):
```cpp
if (trace_mode) {
  log("sel_vec=", sel_scores, "chosen=", chosen_id, "kv_hit=", kv_hit);
}
```

eli: 👍 let's keep those logs rate-limited. We don't want huge telemetry. Maybe sample 1/1000 or enable on canary only.

maria: sampling at 1% in canary. Uploading next nsys after adding sel_vec logs to /shared/traces/1811234620_selvec.qdrep.

jeff: long term: make selector resilient to transient CPU-side delays by including "enqueue_delay" as a feature so it prefers kernels with lower launch overhead when enqueue is delayed. Could be ML-learned or rule-based.

maria: agreed. Filing a short RFC for selector change. For now we'll evaluate canary data and kernel prewarm.

anna: FYI, I also bumped kv-cache GC threshold in dev to reduce sweeps during peak windows. Might help.

maria: thanks all. Will post summary and attach perfetto slices once I correlate selector logs with the nsys timelines. :thumbsup:

jeff: great. If the canary stays good for 4h we'll roll to 50%.

maria: tracking in the ticket: https://redwood.internal/issue/INF-4721 (notes + traces).

eli: closing loop: timeline note — look for pattern: tiny CPU op -> miss launch slot -> generic_matmul -> extra tail. That's our signature.

maria: will include a short script to aggregate that pattern from traces and post results here later today.
